analysis.investment_thesis: Solarium Green is a young (2018) solar EPC/turnkey contractor riding a thematic tailwind, but civil construction and EPC are commoditized, tender-driven, working-capital-heavy businesses with no durable moat. At 21.5x P/E for a 301 Cr micro-cap with a ~3-year public track record, I'd invert and pass — the probability of disappointment far outweighs the visible upside.
key_strengths: ROCE 20.1% and ROE 23% look respectable at current scale
Promoter skin-in-the-game at 58.34% keeps incentives aligned
Structural tailwind from India's solar capacity push
key_risks: Solar EPC is a tender-driven commodity business with zero pricing power
Incorporated 2018 — no cycle-tested track record through a downturn
Working-capital and receivables risk typical of civil construction eats FCF
red_flags: Near-zero institutional ownership (FII 0.22%, DII 3.15%) suggests no serious diligence has validated the story
Industry classification 'Civil Construction' — historically one of the worst ROIC industries in India
Micro-cap EPC with inflated returns often reflects one good order-book year, not durable economics
analysis.detailed_analysis: Inverting first: what kills this investment? Solar EPC and turnkey civil construction is a brutal business — thin margins, L1 tender bidding, long receivables from government/DISCOM counterparties, and capital that gets trapped in work-in-progress. History is littered with Indian infra/EPC names (Suzlon, IVRCL, Punj Lloyd) that posted 20%+ ROCE on the way up, then blew up when the order book turned or working capital exploded. A 2018-incorporated company with 301 Cr market cap has simply not been tested through a full cycle, and I have no basis to believe current ROCE is normalized rather than a point-in-time artifact of a strong solar capex wave.
